2. GOVERNING CONCLUSION
================================================================================
DESIGN_INVALIDATED. The three PRs failed differently but share one cause:

  UNSETTLED CONCEPTS WERE GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS BEFORE THEIR TRUST
  BOUNDARIES WERE PROVEN BY A SMALL NUMBER OF CONCRETE SOURCE-TO-EXECUTION
  EXAMPLES.

Successor work inverts that order. Prove the boundary on five real procedures,
then generalize.

================================================================================
3. CROSS-PR TRUST-BOUNDARY ANALYSIS (the eleven questions)
================================================================================
1. WHO ESTABLISHES THAT A SOURCE OBLIGATION EXISTS?
   UNRESOLVED, and this is the central defect. #475 let the projector carry
   sourceObligations on the same emitted Clause it was judged by; the registry
   that was meant to fix this could not be authoritative because the source
   census underwriting it is deferred (eshyra-s38f). #476 let the pack under
   repair define its own membership. #477 let a hand-written alias table stand
   in. NOTHING in the three PRs independently establishes obligation existence.
   F1 must settle this FIRST.

2. STABLE IDENTITY OF AN OBLIGATION?
   #475 and #477 converged on obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet>. #476 never
   participated — it uses MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?, path?,
   sourceSpan?} with no obligationId. Even where the string shape matched, #477
   minted it for EVIDENCE ITEMS (code-symbol, ownership, primitive-relevance),
   a category error later split into an ev::: namespace. The shape is NOT yet a
   proven identity; treat it as a candidate.

3. WHAT IS AUTHORITATIVE vs MERELY PROJECTED OUTPUT?
   Never cleanly separated. #475's obligations lived beside the projection;
   #476's "derived" rows were generated from the pack being repaired; #477's
   readiness evidence WAS the pack projection. In all three the artifact under
   repair was used as evidence about itself.

4. HOW DOES A PROJECTED ATOM DISCHARGE AN EXACT OBLIGATION?
   UNRESOLVED. #475 evaluated obligations against clause-GLOBAL fields, so one
   save atom could discharge two distinct source saves. The one-obligation-per-
   clause invariant was introduced to dissolve this and is a HYPOTHESIS TO
   RE-TEST in F1, not a settled result.

5. MULTIPLICITY, ALTERNATIVES, OPTION LOCALITY, LIFECYCLE, TIMING, TERMINATION?
   Partially modelled, never proven. Facets existed for duration/recurrence/
   repeatChecks/immunityWindows/termination; alternatives could pass with a
   DISCONNECTED exclusion graph (mutual exclusion is a partition property, and
   one member proves nothing about it). Option locality was asserted, not
   demonstrated. F1 must demonstrate all of these on real procedures.

6. WHAT IDENTITY PERSISTS AFTER A FINDING IS REPAIRED?
   #476 eventually separated a durable obligation+target+invariant from a
   transient violation predicate that may go empty. THAT SEPARATION IS SOUND AND
   SHOULD SURVIVE. What did not survive was the membership behind it.

7. SOURCE-BACKED vs CURRENT-BROKEN-PACK MEMBERSHIP?
   The rule was stated correctly — a row's authority may not be the pack under
   repair — and then not enforced until the final round. An obligation already
   omitted from the pack is invisible to a query over that pack, which is
   exactly the case the registry exists to catch. Ending state: 0 derived,
   68 underived. That zero is the honest measure.

8. EVIDENCE THAT PROVES ONLY PRESENCE / OWNERSHIP / CANDIDACY?
   Exported-symbol existence; bead existence; a record having any engineHooks;
   an alias appearing in a hard-coded universe; a readiness clause existing.
   All four were used as if they proved semantic implementation. They do not.

9. STRONGER EVIDENCE — SEMANTIC IMPLEMENTATION AND PACK-DRIVEN EXECUTION?
   NEVER ACHIEVED in any of the three. This is F4's subject and it must define
   what each category does NOT prove, not only what it does.

10. HOW CAN ABSENCE BE POSITIVELY ESTABLISHED?
    UNRESOLVED and the hardest question. #477 tried invented sentinel markers
    (absence of a made-up token), then anchor-record-only scanning, then closed
    predicates over allowed schemas. The last failed because RulesRecord.data is
    typed unknown and the kind validator does not reject unregistered fields —
    there IS no closed schema to enumerate against. The only sound position
    reached: unclassified structured material must remain UNDERIVED, never
    "absent". Recognising nothing is not evidence of absence.

11. WHICH CONCEPTS MUST STABILIZE FIRST?
    obligation identity + discharge (F1)
      -> exact finding membership (F3)
        -> capability evidence semantics (F4)
          -> bootstrap capability inventory (F5)
    Audit FACTS (F2) may proceed in parallel because they make no executable
    membership claim.

WHERE THE THREE INDEPENDENTLY INVENTED INCOMPATIBLE VERSIONS OF ONE CONCEPT:
  * obligation identity — #475 obl:::(sourceRef,locator,facet) validated against
    evidence; #477 the same string shape but accepting evidence-item facets and
    empty segments; #476 MembershipIdentity with no obligationId at all.
  * evidence taxonomy — #475 ObligationEvidence kinds; #477 a separate
    discriminated union with per-kind resolvers; #476 none.
  * membership — #475 scope closure; #476 baseline vs current vs violation;
    #477 roster + query IDs.
  * capability identity — #475 closed engine:F1..F10 union; #476 a capability
    catalog on the target selector; #477 a roster keyed by primitive.
  * "ready" predicates — THREE independent fail-open implementations.

RECURRING FAILURE IDIOM, five occurrences: returning an empty failure list when
a lookup does not resolve, so "no failures" is indistinguishable from "all
checks passed". Any evaluation path that cannot resolve its input must FAIL.

SECOND RECURRING IDIOM, four occurrences: a required free-text field filled
mechanically to satisfy a validator. Only structured data ended it.

THIRD: count-pinned tests. Asserting the SIZE of a blocker set passes for any
set of that size. Assert identities.

Read in full. F1 started first and alone. No invalidated artifact treated as an

ANSWERS TO SECTION 6 (unresolved design questions for F1) -- proposed, pending review:

Q "Is one-obligation-per-clause correct, or does it merely relocate the multiplicity
   problem into clause decomposition?"
A It RELOCATES it. Replaced by ONE OBLIGATION = ONE FACET OCCURRENCE with `ordinal` in
  the identity: obl/<digest8>/p<page>/q<quoteHash8>/<facetSlot>/<ordinal>. The
  decomposition unit is now the thing being counted, so there is nowhere left to hide
  the problem. Proof case: Burnt Othur Fumes (SRD p.204) has TWO Constitution DC 13
  saves with identical facet content -- obl:::<sourceRef>::<locator>::<facet> cannot
  express them as two. The shipped pack collapses them to mechanics.saves[1 entry].

Q "What creates obligations if the source census does not exist yet -- a curated seed
   for five procedures, or a real extractor?"
A A CURATED, QUOTE-ANCHORED LEDGER for five procedures. Curation alone is untrustworthy
  (that is how #477's alias table failed); what makes it FALSIFIABLE is that every row
  carries a verbatim quote plus the number of occurrences on its cited page, and the
  loader re-derives both from a digest-pinned extraction of the frozen PDF. A curator
  cannot invent an obligation over text that is not there. Completeness is handled
  separately and BOUNDED to five pages by a PageCensus with a mandatory-empty residual.
  Reviewer question Q2.

Q "Can option locality be expressed without a scope/closure layer?"
A YES. Locality is JSON-Pointer containment in the projected record. An obligation with
  locality {kind:'option', optionLabel:'Archery'} is discharged only by an atom whose
  pointer lies under the choices[i].options[j] carrying that label. The projector cannot
  assert scope it does not have. Demonstrated by hoisting Fighting Style's six option
  mechanics to the parent: type-valid, and six LOCALITY_VIOLATIONs.

Q "How is a model-adjudicated boundary represented so it neither satisfies nor blocks?"
A A separate `classification` (deterministic | model-adjudicated | source-ambiguous)
  that fails closed IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: an adjudicated obligation requires an explicit
  in-band declaration (ADJUDICATION_MISSING otherwise) AND forbids a deterministic atom
  covering the same span (ADJUDICATION_SILENTLY_DETERMINIZED); a deterministic
  obligation forbids discharge by an adjudication declaration
  (DETERMINISTIC_DISCHARGED_BY_ADJUDICATION). Proof case Wish (SRD p.193): the
  GM-latitude clause is silently ABSENT today, and mechanics.damage[1d10 necrotic] is
  hoisted out of its stress precondition so it reads as unconditional. NOTE a vocabulary
  gap: the pack's existing RulesAmbiguity (3 records) models SOURCE ambiguity resolvable
  by campaign ruling; Wish needs DESIGNED adjudication with owner 'model'. Extending the
  pack vocabulary is handed to eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4; F1 does not design it.

Q "Does provider-neutral execution require the engine capability registry, or can a
   narrow reference harness prove it for five procedures?"
A A NARROW REFERENCE HARNESS, inside F1. This is also what makes the repointed graph
  non-circular: olc5.1 -> olc5.5 -> 19.1.16 -> 19.1.7 -> 19.1.14 serializes all engine
  work behind F1..F5, so F1 cannot depend on the capability registry to satisfy its own
  real-pack execution acceptance criterion. Recorded as finding D4 so it cannot be
  silently reinterpreted. Reviewer question Q4.

THE THREE RECURRING IDIOMS ARE ADDRESSED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY DISCIPLINE:
 (1) empty failure list on unresolved input -> evaluate() returns Result<Report, Fatal>;
     Report.ok is a derived getter; an empty ledger is Fatal.
 (2) free text filling a validator -> no gate reads any human-facing string field;
     prose atoms fail typedMatch. (Fighting Style's option `text` and Wish's
     description are the live examples.)
 (3) count-pinned tests -> every adversarial test asserts obligation ids, atom ids, or
     failure codes; RC7 makes it reviewable by grepping for .length / toHaveLength.

 * #477 2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md still needs EXTRACTING FIRST so it does
